subject.title: feat(memory): graduate sessionMemory from experimental — solve the multi-session continuity problem

question: What stable contract and default should OpenClaw use for session transcript memory: keep it opt-in, graduate the API/docs without changing defaults, or default it on for new installs after privacy/cost/dedup proof?
rationale: The requested change affects transcript privacy boundaries, config defaults, QMD export behavior, retrieval semantics, costs, and upgrade expectations, which source inspection cannot decide safely without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Keep Opt-In While Stabilizing Contract
options.body: Keep current defaults while resolving source labeling, visibility, duplicate-indexing, QMD export, ranking, cost, and docs requirements, then revisit default-on separately.

options.title: Graduate Without Default-On
options.body: Remove the experimental framing and document a stable opt-in contract while preserving existing user defaults and privacy expectations.

options.title: Default-On For New Installs
options.body: Enable session transcript indexing for new installs only after explicit privacy gates, cost guidance, dedup/ranking proof, and upgrade tests are in place.

recommendation.title: Keep Opt-In While Stabilizing Contract
recommendation.body: Keep current defaults while resolving source labeling, visibility, duplicate-indexing, QMD export, ranking, cost, and docs requirements, then revisit default-on separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the experimental session memory source and is the clearest history-backed owner for the default/stability direction.
